_about: Knowledge base of the DUMMY WM expert researcher (par_generator/wm_expert.py and the preview). Generic, illustrative guidance only: answers are labelled as simulated and must be checked before use.

topics.title: Wave planning
topics.summary: Manual or late wave building usually comes from waves not being driven by templates tied to carrier cut-offs and order priorities. Moving to scheduled, template-based waves is typically a configuration change with a quick payback.
look_at: Wave templates per carrier or cut-off, with order selection criteria and a maximum wave size
Scheduled (automatic) wave runs aligned with the carrier cut-off times
Allocation and deselection rules: why order lines drop out of waves (short stock, in-transit inventory)
Wave release KPIs: lines per wave, deselection rate, time from release to first pick
watch_out: Waves that are too large starve replenishment; too small ones increase travel
Templates need an owner: cut-off times change with carrier contracts
topics.next_step: Map the current cut-offs and order types, build one template per carrier in a lower environment, and compare a week of wave KPIs before and after.

topics.title: Replenishment
topics.summary: Empty pick faces during picking point to min/max replenishment that does not anticipate wave demand. Demand-based (wave-triggered) replenishment, combined with periodic top-offs, usually removes most short picks.
look_at: Replenishment triggered by wave demand in addition to min/max thresholds
Min/max values per item and location, reviewed against recent velocity
Task priority so replenishment tasks are executed before the picks that need them
Multi-pallet or grouped replenishment tasks per aisle to reduce reach-truck travel
watch_out: Demand replenishment without task priorities just moves the problem to the task queue
Pick-face capacity must hold at least one wave's demand for fast movers
topics.next_step: Analyse a week of short picks by item and location, then pilot wave-triggered replenishment on the top fast movers.

topics.title: Picking
topics.summary: Picking productivity is mostly travel: pick sequence, batching of small orders and task grouping are the main levers, and most are configuration rather than development.
look_at: Pick sequence (location sequencing) matching the physical walking path
Cluster or batch picking for small orders, with a cart and container limits
Task grouping and task creation thresholds (avoid one task per line)
Short-pick handling: exception flow and the cycle count it should trigger
watch_out: Changing location sequences invalidates operators' habits: plan a floor walk-through
Cluster picking needs labels or containers that the packing station can read
topics.next_step: Measure travel per line on two shifts, then test a revised pick sequence and cluster picking in one zone.

topics.title: Receiving
topics.summary: Receiving delays usually come from manual steps around the ASN: closing and verifying ASNs by hand, scanning each case of mixed pallets, and new-item messages. Several of these are switches in the receiving configuration.
look_at: Automatic ASN verification and closure once quantities are received
Receiving whole iLPNs or multi-SKU pallets in one scan when the ASN is reliable
Suppressing or simplifying item prompts that slow down each scan
Dock-to-stock time as the KPI to follow
watch_out: One-scan receiving relies on accurate supplier ASNs: check the supplier error rate first
Auto-closure needs a process for late or partial deliveries
topics.next_step: Check ASN accuracy for the main suppliers, then enable the change for the most reliable ones first.

topics.title: Putaway and space
topics.summary: Free or operator-chosen putaway wastes space and travel. Directed putaway with consolidation into partially filled locations and clear zones for returns usually improves both space utilisation and productivity.
look_at: Directed putaway rules per item profile and zone
Consolidation priority into partially filled reserve locations (volume- or quantity-based)
A dedicated returns flow with its own putaway zone and rules
Space utilisation per allocation zone as the follow-up KPI
watch_out: Consolidation can increase putaway travel if not limited to the same aisle or zone
Location dimensions and item dimensions must be accurate for volume-based rules
topics.next_step: Extract location occupancy by zone, then pilot consolidation rules in one reserve zone.

topics.title: Labels and printing
topics.summary: Walking to shared printers is a classic hidden cost. Mapping printers per workstation or dock door, and printing at the right step, is configuration work with an immediate gain.
look_at: Printer mapping per dock door, packing station or user location
Print triggers: at which step each label or document is produced
Customer- or carrier-specific document rules instead of manual reprints
watch_out: Each extra printer needs network, support and consumables: confirm with IT
Test label layouts with the carriers' scanners before go-live
topics.next_step: List print events and walking distances per area, then map the busiest doors and stations first.

topics.title: Packing
topics.summary: Packing speed depends on choosing the right carton up front and on avoiding manual data entry at the station (weights, documents).
look_at: Cartonization at order release so the station knows the carton in advance
Scale integration to capture weights without typing
Packing station flow: scans per order and exception handling
watch_out: Cartonization needs accurate item dimensions
Hardware integration (scales) usually needs a design and testing phase
topics.next_step: Measure time per order at the station and check item dimension quality before enabling cartonization.

topics.title: Shipping and dock
topics.summary: Late or partial trucks usually come from missing capacity planning per trailer type and from appointments that are not managed in the system.
look_at: Shipment planning with capacity per trailer type
Dock appointment scheduling, including recurring appointments for regular carriers
Load closure and shipping confirmation steps that are still manual
watch_out: Appointment scheduling only helps if carriers actually use it: plan the onboarding
Capacity rules need reliable item weights and volumes
topics.next_step: Review a month of late departures by carrier and set up recurring appointments for the top carriers.

topics.title: Inventory accuracy
topics.summary: Inventory accuracy improves most with counts triggered by events (short picks, empty locations) rather than only calendar-based counting.
look_at: Cycle counts triggered by short picks and by locations found empty
Count programmes by ABC class
Adjustment reason codes and their follow-up
watch_out: Event-driven counts add tasks: check counter capacity
Adjustments without reasons hide process problems
topics.next_step: Enable short-pick-triggered counts and review adjustments by reason code after two weeks.

topics.title: Integration
topics.summary: Integration issues (lost or failed messages, late item master updates) are best handled with monitoring and retries before considering development.
look_at: Monitoring and alerting on failed inbound and outbound messages
Retry policies and error queues with an owner on each side
Timing of item master updates versus inbound receipts
watch_out: Fixes often need changes on the ERP side too: involve the client's integration team
Test with production-like volumes in a lower environment
topics.next_step: List the failing message types over a month, agree owners, then set up alerts and retries.

topics.title: Labour and tasks
topics.summary: Supervisors need visibility of work in progress, and equipment should do useful work in both directions: task interleaving and simple dashboards are the usual first steps.
look_at: Task interleaving (putaway and replenishment on the same trip) for reach trucks
Dashboards for backlog per task type and productivity per hour
Engineered or reference standards to compare productivity
watch_out: Interleaving changes task assignment logic: brief the operators
Dashboards need agreed KPI definitions before they are built
topics.next_step: Agree the five KPIs supervisors need, build the dashboard, then pilot interleaving on one shift.

generic.title: General guidance
generic.summary: No specific topic was recognised in the question, so this is the general approach for a PAR finding.
look_at: Whether standard configuration already covers the need before considering extensions
Data quality behind the process (items, locations, ASNs)
The KPI that will show the gain, measured before and after
watch_out: Changes that are critical for productivity need validation on the floor at go-live
generic.next_step: Clarify the expected behaviour with the client's process owner, then test the change in a lower environment.
